question: A PHC medical officer in rural Tamil Nadu notices that the stock of metformin 500 mg tablets is depleted within two weeks of each monthly indent, while atorvastatin 10 mg tablets consistently expire unused. Which action best reflects rational use of the essential medicines framework?

answers.text: Increase the indent quantity for metformin based on documented morbidity data, and review prescribing patterns for atorvastatin against the actual burden of dyslipidaemia in the catchment area

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rational use requires matching indent quantities to evidence of local disease burden (morbidity data for metformin) and auditing over-prescribing or inappropriate selection for atorvastatin — both core EML operational principles.

answers.text: Replace metformin with a newer DPP-4 inhibitor available at district level, as newer drugs are always preferred

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. EML selection favours comparative cost-effectiveness and proven efficacy over novelty. Metformin remains the first-line agent for type 2 diabetes in both the WHO EML and NLEM 2022; switching to a costlier agent without clinical indication is irrational.

answers.text: Dispose of the expired atorvastatin and request the same quantity next month without reviewing indication

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Repeated expiry indicates a mismatch between indent and actual need. Rational use requires auditing whether atorvastatin is being appropriately prescribed and adjusting the indent — not repeating the same over-stock cycle.

answers.text: Submit a complaint to CDSCO about metformin quality, as rapid depletion suggests adulteration

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Rapid depletion indicates high demand (high disease burden), not a quality problem. Quality concerns — such as unusual appearance, patient adverse effects clusters, or failed packaging — would warrant CDSCO/state FDA reporting; demand mismatch does not.

overallFeedback.feedback: Rational use means the right medicine, right dose, right patient, right duration, at the lowest cost. Revisit Block 11 on PHC-level EML application: indent based on morbidity data, audit overstocked items against local disease burden.
Excellent application. Morbidity-data-driven indenting and prescribing audits are the two practical levers for rational essential medicine use at PHC level.
